name: Design of Experiments / A/B Testing
when_to_use: Decide between two or more versions of something (page, email, process) before scaling; random assignment to groups and statistical comparison of the result.
notes: Formalizes how to split groups and measure the outcome so that cause and effect can be claimed with statistical confidence. Applications: test two versions of a page, email or process before scaling.

expected_input.question: How to design and measure an experiment so that cause and effect can be claimed with confidence?

pdca_use: Plan/Check phase: size the sample and statistically compare two versions of an action before scaling — closed-form formulas (proportions/sample size), no model fitting.

plain_explanation.purpose: Compares two randomly assigned versions (A and B) to see which works better, and plans the size of the test.
plain_explanation.when_to_use_plain: When you can randomly choose who sees what.
plain_explanation.data_needed: For each participant, the version received and the outcome (e.g., converted or not).
plain_explanation.example: Test which of two emails gets more replies.
plain_explanation.diagram: audience -> random draw -> version A | version B -> compare rates
